answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a shared contract before it can submit trades; the contract slashes that bond when independent audits prove the agent fabricated a counterparty or duplicated a signed order. A walnut-sized account or a dune of disposable identities does not help: every identity needs separately funded collateral, and the attacker risks losing it on detection. Honest agents can recover bonds after a challenge window, while a relic identity with no stake gains no extra influence.
